summary: Sprint M20 · Input Variables → Auto-Budget → Submit → Approve flow. All 8 requested scenarios verified end-to-end on both backend & frontend. Backend pytest 7 passed / 1 skipped (lifecycle skipped on second run because budget was already Approved — that same lifecycle was fully exercised via the UI). Frontend flow: panel opens with 9 iv-field-* rows, header shows 'Scheme 2-B · Auto-Budget Enabled', default computed total = ₹2,80,800 (matches curl), auto-recompute on match_days 8→10 → ₹3,35,000, iv-head-0 formula updates, save creates Draft budget, submit flips to Submitted (submit button hidden), reload persists inputs, progress-step-budget_created shows done + budget_approved still pending. Inline spec (inter_school) shows 7 fields, no auto-budget preview, save persists to tournament.input_variables without creating a budget. MPCA persona sees disabled inputs + no save/submit buttons but preview still visible. Approved budget shows 'edit locked' badge, all inputs disabled, save button hidden. No blocking issues.

issues: Recurring React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>'. Same finding as iter34 (Emergent visual editor injects <span data-ve-dynamic> inside <option>). Not app-code fault but pollutes console. Also caused a 422 from POST /api/tournaments during UI create for inter_school in this run — I fell back to inserting the tournament directly to test the panel; recommend main agent verify the inter_school create form path in TournamentCreateModal (the modal sent format='OneDay' but backend expects 'One_Day'; also tournament_type default may resolve to 'Domestic_Local' for Invitational-family type_code).

action_items: (Medium) TournamentCreateModal · when Type = inter_school (Invitational family), the POST /api/tournaments payload triggers 422 — the format value 'OneDay' does not match the backend enum ('One_Day') and/or tournament_type mapping is off. Verify the pickType logic in TournamentCreateModal.jsx and the enum bridging so users can actually create an inter_school tournament through the UI. Backend & panel logic themselves are fine — the *create* path is broken for at least this type.

(Optional) Auto-recompute uses a 400ms debounce and cannot be cancelled during a save. Consider adding `if (dirty) return alert('Save first')` before the auto-recompute POSTs a new preview that then races with save — not observed as a bug but a defensive coding improvement.
critical_code_review_comments: InputVariablesPanel.jsx:105 — saveAndUpsertBudget uses window.alert on error. Consider the same heritage-styled inline error area used elsewhere.
InputVariablesPanel.jsx:148 — submitBudget also uses window.confirm/alert. Consistent with existing modal patterns in TournamentWorkspacePanels but modernising to a shadcn Dialog would be preferable.

InputVariablesPanel.jsx:43 — canEdit logic uses `persona?.body_type !== 'State'` AND an allow-list of role ids that already INCLUDES 'secretary'/'president'/'treasurer' (all State roles). Since the body_type check runs first, State personas correctly fall to canEdit=false. The role-id allow-list is redundant for the State personas — either remove them from the list to make the intent explicit, or drop the body_type check. Currently it works because AND short-circuits, but it is easy to misread.

tournament_workspace.py:165 — PATCH /tournaments/{tid}/input-variables returns raw update result with no response model. Consider returning the refreshed tournament document for the frontend to update local state without a second GET.

InputVariablesPanel.jsx:105-144 — After PATCH input-variables, the tournament state in TournamentDetail is refreshed via `onChange?.()` (load()) which is good; but the local `dirty` flag is only cleared after the whole save block completes — if the PATCH succeeds but the POST /tournament-budgets fails (e.g. 409 duplicate), state gets stuck 'dirty' even though inputs were persisted. Consider clearing dirty right after the PATCH succeeds.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Sprint M20 verified complete. Panel workflow states: (1) Fresh tournament with scheme_code → 9 fields render, default total ₹2,80,800, auto-recompute works, iv-head-0 formulas update. (2) Save creates Draft → iv-existing-budget-total appears, iv-budget-status='Draft'. (3) iv-submit-budget-btn present → click → confirm dialog → status Submitted, button hidden. (4) After reload, inputs persist via tournament.input_variables and the panel picks them up (no re-seed of defaults). (5) MPCA persona: all inputs disabled, save/submit buttons hidden, preview still shown for transparency. (6) Approved budget: lock badge 'Budget already approved · edit locked' shown, all inputs disabled, save button hidden. Progress derivation: after budget in Submitted/Approved state, progress-step-budget_created has Check icon and expand-play works. KNOWN OTHER BUG: creating a tournament of type inter_school via the UI modal (TournamentCreateModal) POSTs invalid format ('OneDay' not 'One_Day') and gets 422 — separate to Sprint M20 but blocked me from doing pure end-to-end 'create+open' via UI, so I inserted the doc directly.
rca of the issue: N/A — no blocking issue. Ancillary observation: TournamentCreateModal 422 on inter_school create is caused by the `default_format: 'OneDay'` value in the tournamentCatalog vs the backend Literal enum which requires 'One_Day' (with underscore). Fix by aligning frontend catalog default_format values with backend enums (Multi_Day / One_Day / T20 / …).
